groups.title: DRF Core Concepts
groups.question: You are building a recipes API with Django REST Framework for a React frontend. Explain how serializers, views and permissions work together.

followUps.Serializers and Data Validation: What does a serializer do on the way in and on the way out?
followUps.Views, ViewSets, and Generic Views: When would you use APIView, a generic view or a ViewSet?
followUps.Permissions and Authentication Classes: What is the difference between authentication and permissions in DRF?

evidence.text: It converts model instances into data that can be returned as JSON.
It validates incoming data before saving it.
ModelSerializer generates fields and validation from the model.
APIView gives full control over each HTTP method.
Generic views provide common list and create behaviour with little code.
ViewSets group related actions for one resource in one class.
Authentication works out who is making the request.
Permissions decide what that user is allowed to do.
Object-level permissions check access to a specific record, such as only the owner editing.

notEnough: Only saying DRF has permission classes.

groups.title: API Design Patterns
groups.question: Your recipes endpoint returns ten thousand rows at once and one client sends hundreds of requests per second. Explain how you would paginate, filter and limit requests.

followUps.Pagination and Filtering Strategies: Which pagination style would you choose for a long, frequently updated list?
followUps.Throttling and Rate Limiting APIs: How does throttling protect the API?

evidence.text: DRF offers page number, limit-offset and cursor pagination.
Cursor pagination stays stable and fast when rows are added during browsing.
django-filter adds filtering through query parameters.
Throttling caps how many requests a user or IP can make in a time window.
Separate limits can apply to anonymous and logged-in users.
Clients over the limit get a 429 response.

groups.title: Routing and Browsable API
groups.question: You have several ViewSets and want URLs generated for them and a quick way to try them in the browser. Explain routers and the browsable API.

followUps.Routers and Auto URL Generation: What does a DRF router generate?
followUps.Browsable API for Development: How does the browsable API help during development?

evidence.text: A router creates the standard URL patterns for each ViewSet.
DefaultRouter also adds an API root page.
SimpleRouter is lighter and leaves the root out.
It shows each endpoint as an HTML page in the browser.
You can send requests from forms without a separate tool.
Validation errors are shown in a readable way.

notEnough: Only saying it is a web UI.

groups.title: API Documentation Tooling
groups.question: The frontend team needs accurate API documentation, and you need tests that prove endpoints enforce permissions. Explain how you would document and test the API.

followUps.Auto-Generating OpenAPI Schemas: How would you produce up-to-date API documentation?
followUps.Testing DRF Endpoints with APIClient: How does APIClient help test endpoints?

evidence.text: DRF can generate an OpenAPI schema from your views and serializers.
drf-spectacular gives a more complete schema and Swagger or ReDoc pages.
Generated docs stay in sync with the code.
APIClient sends requests to the API inside tests.
It can authenticate as a specific user.
Tests check status codes and data, including that unauthorized users are refused.
